title: AWS Query not-found, the ErrorResponse envelope's nested Error.Code
why: The body-code carrier's nested row, which only one backend read structurally before #1896. An AWS Query service states its code inside <ErrorResponse><Error><Code>, never at the top level of the body, so a matcher that reads the top level alone sees no code at all and an errorCode clause fails — in five suites at once, while rust-sdk and cli passed. This is IAM's own shape: byte for byte what internal/protocol's WriteQueryXMLError emits for a GetGroup naming a group that does not exist, and what AWS answers but for the xmlns attribute it puts on the root, which no code carrier reads. The body is a string here rather than an object because it is not JSON: the wire is XML, and each suite renders it the way its own stack does, which is what lets the dotnet-sdk suite replay it through a real Query client and see its SDK's XML error unmarshaller resolve the code. The obvious other near miss — a clause naming NoSuchEntityException, which the observed code is a prefix of — is deliberately not among the expectations: the AWS SDK for .NET names IAM's modeled exception class exactly that, so it is a genuine exceptionName surface there and a genuine miss everywhere else. A near miss the corpus cannot state uniformly belongs in a suite's own tests, and near-miss-longer-code pins the rule itself.
